name: transcript-fixer
cost: Free (MIT). An API key is only needed for the optional route without an agent.
works_with: Claude Code (the README's install route). The skill also covers Codex.
short: Fixes speech-to-text mistakes like misheard words and wrong names in meeting notes, lectures and interviews.
what: transcript-fixer cleans up transcripts in two passes. First, a dictionary pass applies corrections you already know. Then your agent reads the whole transcript and fixes one-off errors, checks uncertain names and terms, and saves fixes that keep coming back. It handles Chinese and English homophones and technical terms, and it leaves anything it can't resolve unchanged and queued for review.
who: People who record meetings, lectures or interviews and get messy speech-to-text output, especially mixed Chinese and English. If your transcripts are already clean and you only want minutes, the repo points to its meeting-minutes-taker skill instead.
needs: Claude Code to install the plugin

steps.title: Install the audio suite
steps.text: transcript-fixer only ships in this suite, with speech-to-text, meeting minutes and text-to-speech skills.

steps.title: Run the dictionary pass
steps.text: This alone is not the full job. Then load transcript-fixer so your agent does the whole-transcript pass.

try.label: From the SKILL.md
try.text: Point it at a transcript file and say "fix this transcript". It runs the dictionary pass, then reads the whole thing and corrects what it can back up.

watch: It never rewrites speech for fluency and, by default, never guesses who is speaking. Unresolved wording stays as it was and goes to a review queue.
Before it corrects a person's name it reads your people roster. If that is missing or conflicts, it leaves the name alone.
It keeps its corrections in a SQLite database. The README's `--add` command teaches it new ones.
The optional route without an agent uses the GLM API and needs an API key.
